[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The apparent construction attaches the exception to the clause immediately before it, their remaining in the Fire forever.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p645/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو مسلم | rejects | Abu Muslim attaches the exception to reaching the appointed term, as an exception for those God killed; Abu Hayyan rejects this for its wording, two-term doctrine, and disrupted syntax.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | A disconnected exception can cross time boundaries, as in the statement that they will taste no death there except the first death in the world. | mentions 44:56
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عطية | prefers | Ibn Atiyya's good interpretation makes the exception a present address to the Prophet and community for disbelievers then who God knows will later believe; the next clause supports this sense.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قوم | reports | Another group takes the exception as sinful monotheists who enter the Fire but are not kept there forever.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قوم | reports | A group treats the exception as a period of time, differing over which period is excluded.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الطبري | reports | Al-Tabari identifies the excluded time as the interval from resurrection until their entry into Hell; the wording abode in the Fire does not restrict itself to future time.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari excludes periods when they are transferred from Fire to the torment of freezing cold; a report describes a valley so cold that their limbs separate and they cry to return to Hell.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan takes the exception as their time in the world without punishment; Abu Hayyan says the same objection applies as to excluding people who believed in the world.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says illā means siwā, yielding an exception for whatever increase in punishment God wills; al-Zajjaj approaches this explanation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غيره | reports | Another view excludes punishment beyond the Fire's torment, treating the exception as disconnected from an implied verbal noun for punishment.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p646/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | He says the exception apparently completes God's address to the addressees, as the transmitted interpretations of it indicate.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | يا معشر is accusative under the omitted يقول or قلنا; with al-Zajjaj's passive صيغة, it is nominative as نائب الفاعل.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | prefers | The Shaykh instead parses الذي as an appositive, implicitly الوقت الذي; this makes it generic without a mismatch that would prevent an adjectival analysis.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r11] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفارسي | prefers | Al-Farisi makes خالدين a circumstantial accusative governed by مثواكم, which here is a verbal noun meaning your remaining, not a place noun; he rejects al-Zajjaj's locative gloss.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r12] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Al-Farisi's poetic evidence uses مغار ابن همام as a verbal event; its على complement fits an action rather than a place, supporting his verbal-noun reading of مثوى.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | معشر means a group; an Arabic line uses it for the people from whom the speaker defends others.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النبي | reports | The Prophet's saying نحن معاشر الأنبياء uses معاشر for a class or group, and states that prophets do not leave inheritance.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأودي | reports | Al-Awdi's verse uses معاشر as the plural of معشر, for a group who restore what their people have spoiled.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | من الإنس may be a circumstantial phrase: their allies were human.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively من identifies the kind, since their allies included humans and jinn, with the phrase specifying the human allies.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | ربنا has an omitted vocative particle.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The majority read أجلنا in the singular, matching الذي; an alternative has آجالنا plural while الذي remains singular and masculine.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#2/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو علي | reports | Abu ʿAli treats الذي as generic, with the masculine singular standing for a feminine relative form.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A second possible governor is an omitted verb, يثوون فيها خالدين, with مثواكم understood as the place of remaining.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | rejects | Abu al-Baqa proposes the meaning of the possessive construction as the governor; the author rejects this because the meaning of an iḍāfa cannot govern.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | reports | The majority take the exception from the immediately preceding clause, النار مثواكم خالدين فيها.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو مسلم | reports | Abu Muslim instead makes the exception from their statement that they reached the appointed term: it excludes those whom God seized before that term for disbelief and error.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author rejects Abu Muslim's antecedent: the wording should then be شئت to match أجلت, and the intervening judgment about the fire improperly separates exception from its antecedent.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author also rejects Abu Muslim's interpretation because it assumes two terms, an early term of seizure and a separately appointed term, which he says is disproved elsewhere.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Makkī and Abu al-Baqa in one view call this a disconnected exception: the fire is their abode, except those who believed in worldly life, by analogy with 44:56; the author finds this remote. | mentions 44:56
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#3/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Others regard the exception as connected to the addressed pronoun in مثواكم: those among the group who believed in worldly life are excluded; ما can refer to a rational kind or class. | mentions 4:3
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | For this connected reading, ما can apply to a rational class, as in the Qur'anic phrase فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء. | mentions 4:3
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Al-Hasan al-Basri says the exception is the time they spent in the world before punishment; the author considers this even farther from the preceding readings.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The connected exception is questioned because the unbelievers' future punishment and believers' past worldly faith do not share the same time of judgment, as ordinary exceptions require.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الطبري | reports | Some take the excepted interval as time in the graves; al-Tabari instead makes it the period from resurrection until entry into Hell, since مثواكم need not refer only to the future.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj takes the exception as the combined duration in the graves and the period after resurrection before entering Hell.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says the exception marks intervals when the damned are moved from Hell to a valley of extreme cold that tears their limbs; they howl and ask to return.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Some identify the exception as monotheist sinners who enter Hell but do not remain there forever; ما applies to a category of rational people, and the author says the exception is real and apparent.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The author says this is a genuine exception: the apparent meaning is clear and should not be replaced with a figurative threat that presents an unreal event as real.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as an ironic intensified threat, like a victimized avenger claiming he will relent only if his enemy wishes it.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#4/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's metaphorical account as unnecessary, since the exception has an apparent literal sense.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ, followed by al-Zajjaj, interprets the exception as an increase in punishment; another view says an added form of chastisement, readings that work only as disconnected exceptions.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | The Shaykh parses these as a disconnected exception from the implicit verbal noun: they remain in Hell's punishment except for extra torment beyond the torment denoted by fire.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عطية | reports | Ibn ʿAtiyya says this addresses the Prophet and community, not the Judgment scene: it excludes present unbelievers who God knows will later believe, as indicated by حكيم عليم.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128#5/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The Shaykh calls Ibn ʿAtiyya's reading good, but notes he had earlier called the direct divine address the apparent reading; no strong clue justifies departing from it.
[SAMIN-DURR:6:128/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | يوم may depend on an omitted اذ

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God tells Muhammad to recall this gathering while recounting and warning; the gathered humans are the jinn’s allies who worshipped, sought refuge in, and obeyed them, as they mutually inspired deceptive speech.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The jinn greatly increased their share of humanity by misleading and seducing many, as in the warning that Satan led many people astray. | mentions 36:60, 36:61, 36:62
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatada likewise explain that the jinn misled many humans.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The humans who allied themselves with the jinn respond to God with this explanation of their mutual enjoyment.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says the jinn commanded people and the humans carried out their commands; that was the mutual enjoyment.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · محمد بن كعب | reports | Muhammad ibn Kaʿb glosses their mutual enjoyment as the companions’ enjoyment of one another in worldly life.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن جريج | reports | Ibn Jurayj describes a pre-Islamic man seeking refuge with the chief of a valley; this was the mutual benefit they now cite as an excuse.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p338#3/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Jinn benefited when humans revered and called on them for help; they boasted that they had gained mastery over humans and jinn.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says the appointed term they reached is death.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The fire is the abode and dwelling of the jinn and their human allies, where they remain eternally, subject to God’s will.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · بعضهم | reports | Some say the exception to eternal punishment refers to the period in the barzakh.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · بعضهم | reports | Others say the exception refers to the duration of worldly life; Ibn Kathir postpones fuller treatment of these and other views to 11:107. | mentions 11:107
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p339/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says this verse forbids anyone from deciding for God about His creatures by assigning them to Paradise or Hell.
[NASHR:v1p213/r2] NASHR, d. 833 · author | reports | The author heard that the recitation of Sibt al-Khayyāṭ was so affecting that a group of Jews and Christians embraced Islam after hearing him.
[NASHR:v1p213/r3] NASHR, d. 833 · author | reports | The author names Badr al-Dīn ibn Bakhkhān in Syria and Ibrāhīm al-Ḥakarī in Egypt as the latest reciters he knew to reach the highest level.
[NASHR:v1p213/r4] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | The author says mastery of tajwīd comes from training the tongue and repeatedly practicing the recitation received orally, like improving handwriting through practice and a teacher.
[NASHR:v1p213/r5] NASHR, d. 833 · أبو عمرو الداني | reports | Al-Dānī sums up the role of practice by saying that disciplined exercise is the only difference between tajwīd and neglecting it.
[NASHR:v1p213/r6] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | Correct recitation is not theatrical manipulation of the mouth, jaw, voice, shadda, madd, ghunna, or rāʾ; it should remain easy, sweet, natural, and free of affectation.
[NASHR:v1p213/r7] NASHR, d. 833 · author | holds | The author laments that the path to the highest mastery has now closed and asks God for success and protection from diminished ambition and ignorance.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The gathering day is a central, previously veiled subject of the sūra: its opening alludes to it and later passages repeatedly disclose aspects of it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God gathers every ally and enemy, leaving no one out.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God addresses the jinn through whichever troops He wills to rebuke and humiliate them when they have no power to defend themselves.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Here jinn are hidden, fearsome rebellious devils who gain power over humans and see humans from where humans cannot see them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The jinn sought and achieved a multitude of human followers by leading visible, sociable people astray until most became their adherents.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The verse’s paired wording uses paralleled omission: the jinn’s concealment implies human visibility, while human sociability implies the jinn’s eeriness and aversion.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The human allies’ speech is linked to an omitted jinn response, reconstructed from the dialogue elaborated in the following sūra. | mentions 7:38
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p714/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The past tense presents the dialogue as certain to occur because it is reported by the One who never breaks His promise.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Biqāʿī relates the exchange to the later followers’ blame of their predecessors in the account of the Fire. | mentions 7:38
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The greatest divine name is used to display majesty and guard the divine station, leaving no one able even to contemplate objection.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | He also compares it with the weak followers’ admission that they had followed the arrogant. | mentions 7:75
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The human allies are people who followed and obeyed the jinn in the misguidance they summoned them to.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They say humans enjoyed the jinn’s claims, while the jinn enjoyed human obedience and the humans’ seeking their protection.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | By invoking the appointed term they shift responsibility to destiny: both groups reached death’s decree and jointly denied this day, so both deserve punishment.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Hell is the common home of both groups, and appealing to destiny cannot benefit them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their punishment has no end because they firmly intended to remain in disbelief forever; recompense matches the deed.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Making the punishment’s duration contingent on divine will affirms that God is not bound by any obligation and that His ownership is complete.
[BIQAI-FULL:v2p715/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Biqāʿī says God will not will any end to their punishment; the contingent wording increases their torment by dangling a hope that has no prospect.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains that the jinn greatly increased their number among humans by leading many of them astray.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | On the exception from eternal punishment, Ibn Abbas cautions that no one should decide on God's behalf whether His creatures enter Paradise or Hell.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan understands the jinn's having greatly used mankind as their increasing the number of Hell's people on Judgment Day.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r4] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says the mutual enjoyment consisted in the jinn commanding and humans carrying out their commands.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · محمد بن كعب | reports | Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses their mutual enjoyment as their companionship in worldly life.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · محمد بن كعب | reports | Muhammad ibn Ka'b identifies the appointed term they reached as death.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن جريج | reports | Ibn Jurayj says pre-Islamic men sought a valley's jinn chief's protection when settling there; this was the mutual benefit they cited at the Resurrection.
[DURR-FULL:v3p357/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن جريج | reports | Ibn Jurayj, like Muhammad ibn Ka'b, says the appointed term means death.

[BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The appointed term is the Resurrection; the admission expresses regret and submission after obeying devils, following desire, and denying resurrection.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The Persian verses warn the sleeper to wake before death ends the chance to act: the teacher says they did no work and time has passed.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#2/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The passage quotes only the deluded humans because their corrupters are completely dumbstruck and unable to speak.

[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · صاحب التأويلات النجمية | reports | The exception concerns people who repent and return to God in this life, so Hell will not be their abode; it does not apply to those eternally in Hell.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | One view takes mā as a verbal noun with an omitted genitive, and makes the exception modify the whole preceding statement about eternal residence.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | On this view, the damned may be moved from the fire to a valley of freezing cold that tears their limbs apart; their cries to return to Hell make the exception ironic.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · تفسير الجلالين | reports | Al-Jalālayn explains the exception as periods when they are taken out to drink boiling water, while outside the fire.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | Another view says a door to Paradise opens before the damned; they rush toward it, but it closes as they arrive.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | Another explanation places the exception before entry into Hell, during the delay before admission and eternal residence; outward scholars interpret the exception this way.
[BURSEVI:v3p79#3/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين | reports | Najm al-Dīn alludes to a subtle realization known to those who know God but beyond ordinary understanding, advising that it be disclosed only to spiritual wayfarers.
[BURSEVI:v3p79/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The author prays to be among those on the straight path who reach God's presence with sound hearts and are saved from painful punishment.
[BURSEVI:v3p79/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The verse tells the Prophet to remind Meccans and others of the day God gathers humans and jinn together at the Resurrection and rebukes them.

[BURSEVI:v3p79/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Jinn are named for their concealment from people's sight.
[BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God's wisdom is evident, among other things, in consigning the devils' allies to Hell.
[BURSEVI:v3p80#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God knows the states and deeds of both peoples and the recompense fitting for them.
[ALUSI-FULL:v8p25/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | يوم is an adverb with an implied governing verb such as اذكر, تقول, or كان ما لا يذكر لفظاعته; alternatively it is the object of an omitted verb such as اذكر ذلك اليوم.
